rule: R7 Wait-and-confirm: after an R1 trigger (first c/w look 2-360 min before the start with listed EV >= 2.5%) wait 5 minutes and buy only if the bet is still listed with EV still >= 2.5% (builder verdict: NO GAIN)

reason: Reproduces to the digit (77 bets, 28 games, 52 closes, CLV +2.93%, ROI -16.1%, halves 2.32% | 3.06%), and the builder's own conclusion (no gain) is correct and, if anything, understated. The only evidence for R7 is a +0.4 pt difference (vs not-confirmed +0.41 [-1.59, +1.83]; vs R1 +0.39 [-0.62, +1.22]) that is about one fifth of its own standard error (SE about 0.87 pts on 25 vs 32 games), is not stable across date halves (-0.11 pts | +0.49 pts vs R1; -0.41 | +0.58 vs not-confirmed), and vanishes (-0.08 pts) once confirmed and not-confirmed bets are compared on the same kind of close (R7 has 73% Tracker closes vs 58%, and Tracker closes run 2.7 pts higher than independent ones in R1); on independent closes the confirmed bets are WORSE (-0.26% on 12 vs +1.42% on 21). The cost is certain: R7 forgoes 58% of R1's bets (34 vs 82 a day), 52% of daily CLV-points (about 100 vs 208) and every dropped stratum still has positive CLV (+2.1% to +3.7%); 18 of the 77 confirmed bets (23%) were listed at T only by the study's wide read or Vigilant's scan, not the app's CNO list (the app's alerts and auto-bet never read the wide read), and 47% of confirmed bets (36 of 77) were hidden by Tj's CNO filters at first look. Settling a +0.4 pt effect would take about 1,850 confirmed closes (about 890 games, roughly 80 days at the study's pace); no volume trade is worth that. Not a credible improvement to put to Tj as a change to what the app buys.
caveats: Sample: 2.26 days of first-looks; R7 CLV rests on 52 closes in 25 games; 25 of the 77 confirmed have no close (not yet played at the file's cut Oct 6 00:05, or no close source). Closes are censored by time: Oct 5 triggers have closes on only 18 of 57.

The trigger-day 'first half' is Oct 3 evening only (26 R1 triggers, 9 R7 closes, 7 games): it is not a usable half. The loader's split_by_date puts only 6 R7 closes / 3 games in the second half. No split gives an out-of-sample half with more than 18 games and every half has a CI that spans zero for the difference.
App versions differ by day (Oct 3-4 triggers are v0.57-0.61, Oct 5 triggers v0.66-0.68; presets '2 (Safe CLV)' and 'Volume + safe CLV'), so date halves are also version halves.

Tracker closes (CNO's books read before the start, for bets Tj also placed) are not independent of the listing's own fair: Tracker CLV +3.49% (75 closes) vs independent +0.81% (33 closes) across R1, so R1's own edge may be nearer +1% than +2.5%; confirmation correlates with Tj placing the bet, which is what produces a Tracker close.

My category counts differ from the builder's (63 dropped / 8 too close vs 55 / 16) because 'too close' is tested at T versus at the price look; the confirmed set (77) is the same. One confirmed bet is kept 'listed' only by a Vigilant look 80 minutes old after CNO dropped it (no close, so no CLV effect; ROI -14.9% without it).

Look-ahead check: confirmation state uses looks with t <= trigger+5 min only (x-looks replayed per source), price is the last c/w price look at or before T (median 2 min old, max 5); CLV uses the close only as the outcome. No look-ahead found. Looks are logged to the whole minute and only 'at least every 5 minutes while listed', so 'still listed' at T can rest on a look up to 5 minutes old (3 triggers had a freshest listing look older than 7 min at T; 1 of them counts as confirmed).

The price bought is a logged CNO price, not a fill: R7 assumes the price at the last look is still takeable at T; with median Novig dollars at the price of $40 (mean $314) and only 9% of confirmed bets showing any price change, real fills would be smaller than the study's unit.

Any rule change to what the app buys is a QUESTION FOR TJ; this analysis recommends no change and no loosening of any safety limit. Shorter confirmation (1-2 min) is a different hypothesis (nominal p 0.02 but mix-adjusted p 0.06-0.07 and 9 wait lengths tried); if Tj wants it tested, it needs a pre-registered 1-minute persistence check logged next time, not a rule change now.
